title: Inside the mind of a master procrastinator
speaker: Tim Urban

sentences.en: So in college, I was a government major, which means I had to write a lot of papers.
sentences.zh: 所以在大学里，我学的是政府专业，这意味着我必须写很多论文。

sentences.en: Now, when a normal student writes a paper, they might spread the work out a little like this.
sentences.zh: 现在，当一个普通学生写论文时，他们可能会像这样展开工作。

sentences.en: So, you know -- (Laughter) you get started maybe a little slowly, but you get enough done in the first week that, with some heavier days later on, everything gets done, things stay civil.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道——（笑声）你开始的时候可能有点慢，但是你在第一周就完成了足够的事情，在接下来的几天里，一切都完成了，一切都保持文明。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And I would want to do that like that.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我也想那样做。

sentences.en: That would be the plan. I would have it all ready to go, but then, actually, the paper would come along, and then I would kind of do this.
sentences.zh: 这就是计划。我会把一切准备好，然后，实际上，论文会出现，然后我就会这样做。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And that would happen every single paper.
sentences.zh: （笑声）每一篇论文都会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: But then came my 90-page senior thesis, a paper you're supposed to spend a year on.
sentences.zh: 但接下来是我 90 页的高级论文，你应该花一年的时间来完成这篇论文。

sentences.en: And I knew for a paper like that, my normal work flow was not an option.
sentences.zh: 我知道对于这样的论文，我的正常工作流程不是一个选择。

sentences.en: It was way too big a project. So I planned things out, and I decided I kind of had to go something like this.
sentences.zh: 这是一个太大的工程。所以我计划好了事情，我决定我必须这样做。

sentences.en: This is how the year would go. So I'd start off light, and I'd bump it up in the middle months, and then at the end, I would kick it up into high gear just like a little staircase.
sentences.zh: 这一年就这样过去了。所以我会从灯光开始，在中间几个月我会提高它，然后在最后，我会把它踢到高速档，就像一个小楼梯一样。

sentences.en: How hard could it be to walk up the stairs?
sentences.zh: 走上楼梯有多难？

sentences.en: No big deal, right? But then, the funniest thing happened.
sentences.zh: 没什么大不了的，对吧？但随后，最有趣的事情发生了。

sentences.en: Those first few months? They came and went, and I couldn't quite do stuff.
sentences.zh: 最初几个月？他们来来去去，我却无能为力。

sentences.en: So we had an awesome new revised plan. (Laughter) And then -- (Laughter) But then those middle months actually went by, and I didn't really write words, and so we were here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个很棒的新修订计划。 （笑声）然后——（笑声）但是中间的几个月实际上过去了，我并没有真正写下文字，所以我们就在这里。

sentences.en: And then two months turned into one month, which turned into two weeks.
sentences.zh: 然后两个月变成了一个月，又变成了两周。

sentences.en: And one day I woke up with three days until the deadline, still not having written a word, and so I did the only thing I could: I wrote 90 pages over 72 hours,
sentences.zh: 有一天，我醒来，距离截止日期还有三天，仍然没有写一个字，所以我做了我唯一能做的事：我在 72 小时内写了 90 页，

sentences.en: pulling not one but two all-nighters -- humans are not supposed to pull two all-nighters -- sprinted across campus, dove in slow motion, and got it in just at the deadline.
sentences.zh: 不是一个人，而是两个人通宵——人类不应该通宵达旦——冲刺穿过校园，以慢动作潜入，并在截止日期前完成。

sentences.en: I thought that was the end of everything.
sentences.zh: 我以为一切就这样结束了。

sentences.en: But a week later I get a call, and it's the school.
sentences.zh: 但一周后我接到电话，是学校打来的。

sentences.en: And they say, "Is this Tim Urban?" And I say, "Yeah."
sentences.zh: 他们说：“这是蒂姆·厄本吗？”我说：“是的。”

sentences.en: And they say, "We need to talk about your thesis."
sentences.zh: 他们说：“我们需要谈谈你的论文。”

sentences.en: And I say, "OK." And they say, "It's the best one we've ever seen."
sentences.zh: 我说：“好吧。”他们说：“这是我们见过的最好的一个。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) That did not happen.
sentences.zh: （笑声）（掌声）那没有发生。

sentences.en: (Laughter) It was a very, very bad thesis.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 这是一篇非常非常糟糕的论文。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I just wanted to enjoy that one moment when all of you thought, "This guy is amazing!"
sentences.zh: （笑声）我只是想享受那一刻，当你们所有人都想“这家伙太棒了！”

sentences.en: (Laughter) No, no, it was very, very bad.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 不，不，那是非常非常糟糕的。

sentences.en: Anyway, today I'm a writer-blogger guy. I write the blog Wait But Why.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，今天我是一个作家兼博主。我写了博客“Wait But Why”。

sentences.en: And a couple of years ago, I decided to write about procrastination.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我决定写一篇关于拖延症的文章。

sentences.en: My behavior has always perplexed the non-procrastinators around me, and I wanted to explain to the non-procrastinators of the world what goes on in the heads of procrastinators, and why we are the way we are.
sentences.zh: 我的行为总是让我周围的非拖延者感到困惑，我想向世界上的非拖延者解释拖延者的脑子里在想什么，以及为什么我们是这样的。

sentences.en: Now, I had a hypothesis that the brains of procrastinators were actually different than the brains of other people.
sentences.zh: 现在，我有一个假设：拖延者的大脑实际上与其他人的大脑不同。

sentences.en: And to test this, I found an MRI lab that actually let me scan both my brain and the brain of a proven non-procrastinator, so I could compare them.
sentences.zh: 为了测试这一点，我找到了一个 MRI 实验室，它实际上可以让我扫描我的大脑和经过验证的非拖延者的大脑，这样我就可以对它们进行比较。

sentences.en: I actually brought them here to show you today.
sentences.zh: 我今天实际上把它们带到这里来给你们看。

sentences.en: I want you to take a look carefully to see if you can notice a difference.
sentences.zh: 我希望你仔细看一下，看看你是否能注意到差异。

sentences.en: I know that if you're not a trained brain expert, it's not that obvious, but just take a look, OK?
sentences.zh: 我知道，如果你不是受过训练的大脑专家，这不是那么明显，但看看吧，好吗？

sentences.en: So here's the brain of a non-procrastinator.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不拖延者的大脑。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now ... here's my brain. (Laughter) There is a difference.
sentences.zh: （笑声）现在……这是我的大脑。 （笑声） 是有区别的。

sentences.en: Both brains have a Rational Decision-Maker in them, but the procrastinator's brain also has an Instant Gratification Monkey.
sentences.zh: 两个大脑中都有一个理性决策者，但拖延者的大脑中也有一个即时满足猴。

sentences.en: Now, what does this mean for the procrastinator?
sentences.zh: 现在，这对拖延者意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, it means everything's fine until this happens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着在这件事发生之前一切都很好。

sentences.en: [This is a perfect time to get some work done.] [Nope!]
sentences.zh: [这是完成一些工作的最佳时机。] [不！]

sentences.en: So the Rational Decision-Maker will make the rational decision to do something productive, but the Monkey doesn't like that plan, so he actually takes the wheel, and he says, "Actually, let's read the entire Wikipedia page
sentences.zh: 因此，理性决策者会做出理性的决定，去做一些富有成效的事情，但猴子不喜欢这个计划，所以他实际上掌握了方向盘，他说：“实际上，让我们阅读整个维基百科页面

sentences.en: of the Nancy Kerrigan/ Tonya Harding scandal, because I just remembered that happened.
sentences.zh: 南希·克里根/托尼亚·哈丁丑闻，因为我刚刚记得发生过那件事。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Then -- (Laughter) Then we're going to go over to the fridge, to see if there's anything new in there since 10 minutes ago.
sentences.zh: （笑声）然后——（笑声）然后我们要去冰箱看看，看看里面有没有 10 分钟前的新东西。

sentences.en: After that, we're going to go on a YouTube spiral that starts with videos of Richard Feynman talking about magnets and ends much, much later with us watching interviews with Justin Bieber's mom.
sentences.zh: 之后，我们将在 YouTube 上进行螺旋式播放，从理查德·费曼 (Richard Feynman) 谈论磁铁的视频开始，到很久以后我们观看贾斯汀·比伯 (Justin Bieber) 妈妈的采访结束。

sentences.en: (Laughter) "All of that's going to take a while, so we're not going to really have room on the schedule for any work today.
sentences.zh: （笑声）“所有这些都需要一段时间，所以我们今天的日程安排上不会有足够的空间来进行任何工作。

sentences.en: Sorry!" (Sigh) Now, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 抱歉！”（叹气）现在，这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: The Instant Gratification Monkey does not seem like a guy you want behind the wheel.
sentences.zh: 即时满足猴看起来不像是你想要的驾驶者。

sentences.en: He lives entirely in the present moment.
sentences.zh: 他完全活在当下。

sentences.en: He has no memory of the past, no knowledge of the future, and he only cares about two things: easy and fun.
sentences.zh: 他对过去没有记忆，对未来一无所知，他只关心两件事：轻松和有趣。

sentences.en: Now, in the animal world, that works fine.
sentences.zh: 现在，在动物世界中，这很有效。

sentences.en: If you're a dog and you spend your whole life doing nothing other than easy and fun things, you're a huge success!
sentences.zh: 如果你是一只狗，一生只做简单有趣的事情，那么你就取得了巨大的成功！

sentences.en: (Laughter) And to the Monkey, humans are just another animal species.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 对于猴子来说，人类只是另一种动物。

sentences.en: You have to keep well-slept, well-fed and propagating into the next generation, which in tribal times might have worked OK.
sentences.zh: 你必须保持良好的睡眠、良好的饮食并繁衍下一代，这在部落时代可能会很有效。

sentences.en: But, if you haven't noticed, now we're not in tribal times.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你没有注意到，现在我们并不是处于部落时代。

sentences.en: We're in an advanced civilization, and the Monkey does not know what that is.
sentences.zh: 我们处在一个先进的文明中，而猴子不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: Which is why we have another guy in our brain, the Rational Decision-Maker, who gives us the ability to do things no other animal can do.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们的大脑中有另一个人，理性决策者，他让我们有能力做其他动物做不到的事情。

sentences.en: We can visualize the future. We can see the big picture.
sentences.zh: 我们可以想象未来。我们可以看到大局。

sentences.en: We can make long-term plans. And he wants to take all of that into account.
sentences.zh: 我们可以制定长期计划。他想把所有这些都考虑在内。

sentences.en: And he wants to just have us do whatever makes sense to be doing right now.
sentences.zh: 他想让我们做任何现在有意义的事情。

sentences.en: Now, sometimes it makes sense to be doing things that are easy and fun, like when you're having dinner or going to bed or enjoying well-earned leisure time.
sentences.zh: 现在，有时做一些简单而有趣的事情是有意义的，比如当你吃晚饭、睡觉或享受应得的休闲时间时。

sentences.en: That's why there's an overlap. Sometimes they agree.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么会有重叠。有时他们会同意。

sentences.en: But other times, it makes much more sense to be doing things that are harder and less pleasant, for the sake of the big picture.
sentences.zh: 但其他时候，为了大局考虑，做一些更困难、更不愉快的事情更有意义。

sentences.en: And that's when we have a conflict. And for the procrastinator, that conflict tends to end a certain way every time, leaving him spending a lot of time in this orange zone, an easy and fun place that's entirely out of the Makes Sense circle.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们发生冲突的时候。对于拖延者来说，这种冲突每次都会以某种方式结束，让他花很多时间在这个橙色区域，一个简单而有趣的地方，完全超出了“有意义”圈子。

sentences.en: I call it the Dark Playground. (Laughter) Now, the Dark Playground is a place that all of you procrastinators out there know very well.
sentences.zh: 我称之为黑暗游乐场。 （笑声）现在，黑暗游乐场是你们所有拖延症患者都非常熟悉的地方。

sentences.en: It's where leisure activities happen at times when leisure activities are not supposed to be happening.
sentences.zh: 这是在不应该进行休闲活动的时候进行休闲活动的地方。

sentences.en: The fun you have in the Dark Playground isn't actually fun, because it's completely unearned, and the air is filled with guilt, dread, anxiety, self-hatred -- all of those good procrastinator feelings.
sentences.zh: 你在黑暗游乐场中获得的乐趣实际上并不有趣，因为它完全是不劳而获的，空气中充满了内疚、恐惧、焦虑、自我憎恨——所有这些都是拖延者的良好感受。

sentences.en: And the question is, in this situation, with the Monkey behind the wheel, how does the procrastinator ever get himself over here to this blue zone, a less pleasant place, but where really important things happen?
sentences.zh: 问题是，在这种情况下，猴子在开车，拖延者如何让自己来到这个蓝色区域，一个不太令人愉快的地方，但真正重要的事情发生的地方？

sentences.en: Well, turns out the procrastinator has a guardian angel, someone who's always looking down on him and watching over him in his darkest moments -- someone called the Panic Monster.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，拖延者有一个守护天使，一个总是瞧不起他并在他最黑暗的时刻守护着他的人——一个叫做恐慌怪物的人。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, the Panic Monster is dormant most of the time, but he suddenly wakes up anytime a deadline gets too close
sentences.zh: （笑声）现在，恐慌怪物大部分时间都处于休眠状态，但每当截止日期临近时他就会突然醒来

sentences.en: or there's danger of public embarrassment, a career disaster or some other scary consequence.
sentences.zh: 或者存在公众尴尬、职业灾难或其他可怕后果的危险。

sentences.en: And importantly, he's the only thing the Monkey is terrified of.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，他是猴子唯一害怕的东西。

sentences.en: Now, he became very relevant in my life pretty recently, because the people of TED reached out to me about six months ago and invited me to do a TED Talk.
sentences.zh: 现在，他最近在我的生活中变得非常重要，因为大约六个月前 TED 的人联系了我并邀请我做一场 TED 演讲。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, of course, I said yes. It's always been a dream of mine to have done a TED Talk in the past.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 现在，我当然答应了。参加 TED 演讲一直是我的梦想。

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) But in the middle of all this excitement,
sentences.zh: （笑声）（掌声）但是在这一切兴奋之中，

sentences.en: the Rational Decision-Maker seemed to have something else on his mind.
sentences.zh: 理性决策者似乎还有别的想法。

sentences.en: He was saying, "Are we clear on what we just accepted?
Do we get what's going to be now happening one day in the future?
We need to sit down and work on this right now."

And the Monkey said, "Totally agree, but let's just open Google Earth and zoom in to the bottom of India, like 200 feet above the ground, and scroll up for two and a half hours til we get to the top of the country, so we can get a better feel for India."
(Laughter) So that's what we did that day.
(Laughter) As six months turned into four and then two and then one, the people of TED decided to release the speakers.
And I opened up the website, and there was my face staring right back at me.
And guess who woke up? (Laughter) So the Panic Monster starts losing his mind, and a few seconds later, the whole system's in mayhem.
(Laughter) And the Monkey -- remember, he's terrified of the Panic Monster -- boom, he's up the tree!
And finally, the Rational Decision-Maker can take the wheel and I can start working on the talk.
Now, the Panic Monster explains all kinds of pretty insane procrastinator behavior, like how someone like me could spend two weeks unable to start the opening sentence of a paper,
and then miraculously find the unbelievable work ethic to stay up all night and write eight pages.
And this entire situation, with the three characters -- this is the procrastinator's system.
It's not pretty, but in the end, it works.
This is what I decided to write about on the blog a couple of years ago.
When I did, I was amazed by the response.
Literally thousands of emails came in, from all different kinds of people from all over the world, doing all different kinds of things.
These are people who were nurses, bankers, painters, engineers and lots and lots of PhD students.
(Laughter) And they were all writing, saying the same thing: "I have this problem too."
But what struck me was the contrast between the light tone of the post and the heaviness of these emails.
These people were writing with intense frustration about what procrastination had done to their lives, about what this Monkey had done to them.
And I thought about this, and I said, well, if the procrastinator's system works, then what's going on?
Why are all of these people in such a dark place?
Well, it turns out that there's two kinds of procrastination.
Everything I've talked about today, the examples I've given, they all have deadlines.
And when there's deadlines, the effects of procrastination are contained to the short term because the Panic Monster gets involved.
But there's a second kind of procrastination that happens in situations when there is no deadline.

So if you wanted a career where you're a self-starter -- something in the arts, something entrepreneurial -- there's no deadlines on those things at first, because nothing's happening, not until you've gone out and done the hard work

to get momentum, get things going. There's also all kinds of important things outside of your career that don't involve any deadlines, like seeing your family or exercising and taking care of your health, working on your relationship
or getting out of a relationship that isn't working.
Now if the procrastinator's only mechanism of doing these hard things is the Panic Monster, that's a problem, because in all of these non-deadline situations, the Panic Monster doesn't show up.
He has nothing to wake up for, so the effects of procrastination, they're not contained; they just extend outward forever.
And it's this long-term kind of procrastination that's much less visible and much less talked about than the funnier, short-term deadline-based kind.
It's usually suffered quietly and privately.
And it can be the source of a huge amount of long-term unhappiness, and regrets.
And I thought, that's why those people are emailing, and that's why they're in such a bad place.
It's not that they're cramming for some project.
It's that long-term procrastination has made them feel like a spectator, at times, in their own lives.
The frustration is not that they couldn't achieve their dreams; it's that they weren't even able to start chasing them.
So I read these emails and I had a little bit of an epiphany -- that I don't think non-procrastinators exist.
That's right -- I think all of you are procrastinators.

Now, you might not all be a mess, like some of us, (Laughter) and some of you may have a healthy relationship with deadlines, but remember: the Monkey's sneakiest trick is when the deadlines aren't there.
Now, I want to show you one last thing. I call this a Life Calendar.
That's one box for every week of a 90-year life.
That's not that many boxes, especially since we've already used a bunch of those.
So I think we need to all take a long, hard look at that calendar.
We need to think about what we're really procrastinating on, because everyone is procrastinating on something in life.
We need to stay aware of the Instant Gratification Monkey.
That's a job for all of us. And because there's not that many boxes on there, it's a job that should probably start today.
Well, maybe not today, but ... (Laughter) You know.
Sometime soon. Thank you. (Applause)
